disposition_reason: Reports one lead and one cadmium value for each of five farm vegetables sampled at harvest in Faridabad, printed in percent units that conflict with the text.

study.design: cross-sectional field sampling of five vegetables and the soil under each crop
study.origin: farmland at five locations in Faridabad, Haryana, India (Khedi gujran, Kabulpur, Sector 56, Sector 89, Old Faridabad); described as contaminated farmland in an industrial district
study.method: ICP-MS (contract testing laboratory, Faridabad); digestion not described
study.qa: no CRM, recovery or blank reported

findings.group: farmland at harvest, Khedi gujran, Faridabad (V1)
findings.integrity_flag: Unit conflict: Table 4 prints this vegetable result in percent (0.03 to 0.09 %, i.e. 300 to 900 mg/kg), but the text calls the vegetable lead values below the EU 0.3 mg/kg limit and cadmium below FAO/WHO food limits; value not converted
findings.notes: One composite 1 kg sample per location; edible part washed and ground; percent unit kept unconverted because it contradicts the paper's own limit comparison. Paired soil under the crop: see Table 4 (soil not recorded as a finding).

unresolved: All vegetable values are printed in percent (0.03 to 0.09 %), which equals 300 to 900 mg/kg; the text states they are below the EU 0.3 mg/kg lead limit and FAO/WHO cadmium limits, so the true unit is unknown and no ug/kg value is stored.

Section 3.6 gives vegetable cadmium as 0.03, 0.07, 0.07, 0.06, 0.03 % (the lead series) while Table 4 gives 0.04, 0.09, 0.06, 0.08, 0.04 %; the discussion also gives soil cadmium as 1.77 to 1.82 % (the soil lead range) against Table 4 soil cadmium 1.52 to 2.90 %.
Keywords mention a target hazard quotient but no THQ values are printed.
Single composite sample per vegetable; fresh or dry basis not stated.
Manifest note called this a market survey; the paper samples farmland at harvest.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU lead limit for vegetables cited
